mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods following a UNRATE increase, or the Rank IC for UNRATE and SPX returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above a 5-month moving average signals strong demand in the housing market, which may boost related industries and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 5% from its 5-month moving average
failure_condition: Housing starts increase by more than 5%, but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the following 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests increased economic activity, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by more than 2% year-over-year
failure_condition: Industrial production grows by more than 2% YoY, but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDP growth slows and unemployment rises, but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary tightening cycle may increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 25 basis points in a single hike
failure_condition: The federal funds rate increases by more than 25 basis points, but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weak consumer demand, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by more than 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: Retail sales decline by more than 2% MoM, but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) without a corresponding increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) may indicate a mismatch in monetary policy, leading to increased uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressures without corresponding rate hikes
failure_condition: CPI increases by more than 3% YoY and FEDFUNDS does not increase by more than 25 basis points, but the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Non-farm payroll increases by more than 100,000, but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of cases.
